prerequisite_handlers_checked.detail: No dedicated CER Request handler exists in elisa-dra; command 257 is classified base-protocol by isBaseProtocol (lines 30-38) and onCorsacIngress (CorsacPeerFabric lines 233-240) returns immediately. No AVP 'avp-length' or V-flag header-size validation is performed.
CEA path only transitions PeerState to OPEN and records advertised application ids (PeerConnection.ceaAccepted lines 48-57). No AVP length/vendor validation of the wire framing.
Empty-string placeholder in the prerequisite list; no corresponding message or handler in the codebase.

results.evidence: DiameterWireCodec.decode (lines 89-116) validates avpLength only against the 8-byte base header (line 93: avpLength < AVP_HEADER_LENGTH). When FLAG_V (0x80) is set, line 96 unconditionally reads a 4-byte Vendor-Id (12-byte header) but dataLength=avpLength-8-4 (line 98, clamped >=0 at line 99) and offset advances by pad(avpLength) (line 115). For avp-length in [8..11] with V set, the decoder consumes a 12-byte header while advancing offset by only 8-12 bytes, over-reading relative to the declared Diameter 'length' and, for a trailing AVP at the message boundary, past the buffer (Netty IndexOutOfBoundsException). The prerequisite CER/CEA (Capabilities Exchange, command 257) path does not pre-validate this: isBaseProtocol/onCorsacIngress short-circuit base-protocol messages before any AVP inspection, peer state transitions (ceaAccepted) carry no framing validation, and there are no CapabilitiesExchangeRequest/Answer handler classes in elisa-dra. The 12-byte vendor-header rule is applied correctly only in the separate bench module (DiaWire.decodeAvps, hdr = vendorFlag ? 12 : 8), not in the production codec. The missing validation is therefore absent on the reachable decode path.
